**Campanile 0.1: a neighborhood information and help point that keeps working when the internet is gone.**

A laptop or a Raspberry Pi becomes a local Wi-Fi network. Anyone nearby connects with their own
phone, no app and no account, and finds official notices, an "I offer / I need" board, an
"I'm safe" registry, an offline map and offline medical articles from Wikipedia.

**What's inside**

- **An offline map of the world, and your area street by street.** The setup page frames where
  the computer is. Search a street, a town or a shop, or tap **Hospital, Pharmacy, Water,
  Police** to see the nearest. All of it works without internet.
- **A navigator, without internet.** Pick a destination on the map and get the line to follow,
  on foot or by car, with the turns. Whoever runs the Campanile can mark a flooded or collapsed
  street on the admin page. Every route then avoids it, and it shows in red on everyone's map.
  It's a guide, not a promise, so the date of the map data is shown under every route.
- **Wikipedia's medical articles in Italian, English or both**, readable offline.
- **More Campaniles without internet.** Copy a prepared Campanile to a USB stick, together with
  Python's official installers, and it starts on another computer with nothing installed. Maps
  and Wikipedia can also travel over Wi-Fi between Campaniles, signed with a code read in person.
- **Security reviews.** Our own reviews, done as attackers, found real flaws. Each one is fixed and
  covered by a test that fails on the old code: request smuggling through nginx, a USB stick
  prepared to hide a program in the copy, maps made to exhaust memory, DNS rebinding, a wide
  bridge that one touch closed on one side only. There has been no external audit yet.

**Download:** `campanile-0.1.0.zip` below. Unzip it, then double-click *Avvia Campanile (Windows)*
or *Avvia Campanile (Mac)*. The first time, a setup page downloads the map and the medical
articles. For a Raspberry Pi, see docs/SETUP.md.

**Experimental.** Tested on macOS, Windows and Linux and on a real iPhone, and load-tested with up
to 1,000 simulated phones. **Not yet field-tested:** the Raspberry Pi hotspot, Android, many real
phones at once. What we tested and what we couldn't: [docs/TESTING.md](https://github.com/Carrotstudiosoftwarehouse/campanile/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md).
If you can test those parts, please tell us how it went.

---

**Campanile 0.1: un punto di informazione e aiuto di quartiere che funziona anche senza internet.**
Bacheca, avvisi, "sto bene", mappa del mondo e della tua zona con la ricerca, un navigatore a
piedi e in auto che evita le strade interrotte, Wikipedia medica in italiano e in inglese, tutto
senza internet. Si copia su chiavetta, e mappe e Wikipedia passano via Wi-Fi da un Campanile
all'altro. Scarica `campanile-0.1.0.zip`, scompatta e fai doppio clic su *Avvia Campanile
(Windows)* o *(Mac)*. È una versione sperimentale: cosa abbiamo provato e cosa no è in
[docs/PROVE.md](https://github.com/Carrotstudiosoftwarehouse/campanile/blob/main/docs/PROVE.md).
